papers.title: A data-driven approach for learning traffic assignment using an artificial neural network
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Transport
papers.abstract: Solving transportation network design problems using traffic assignment models becomes increasingly impractical as the size of the considered network grows, due to the need to evaluate numerous candidate solutions. This study aims to model the traffic assignment process through a data-driven approach, and introduces a model based on an artificial neural network (ANN) to predict the total travel time in a network under various link capacity modifications for a specified set of links. ANN-based prediction models are trained and validated on a synthetic data set generated from a medium-sized network to evaluate the feasibility of the proposed approach. Models developed using different ANN architectures highlight the importance of selecting the most suitable architecture specific to the problem. The practical value of the ANN-based prediction model becomes apparent when used in optimising a transportation network design problem instead of the traditional traffic-assignment model: the ANN-based model reduced by up to 60 000 times the computation time required for the optimisation.

papers.title: Digital twin in design architecture: Impact of DT in architectural design for improved building lifecycle management
papers.journal: Journal of Information Technology in Construction
papers.abstract: Digital twins (DTs) are increasingly transforming the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry by enhancing data integration, visualization, collaboration, and decision-making throughout the building lifecycle. Despite these advances, limited research has examined the role of DTs in supporting architectural design for improved Building Lifecycle Management (BLM), particularly during the early design stages. This study investigates the potential of DT technology to enhance BLM by integrating digital twin concepts into the architectural design process. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining a comprehensive literature review with a questionnaire survey of 60 architecture, engineering, and construction professionals from Saudi Arabia, Nigeria, and the United States to evaluate current awareness, perceived benefits, implementation challenges, and opportunities associated with DT adoption. The findings indicate that while awareness of DT technology is increasing, its application to architectural design for comprehensive BLM remains limited. The study identifies key opportunities for improving decision-making, sustainability, lifecycle performance, and stakeholder collaboration, while highlighting workforce skills, interoperability, and implementation complexity as major barriers to adoption. By integrating literature-based evidence with industry perspectives, the research clarifies how design-stage decisions, digital information, and lifecycle requirements can be connected more effectively through DT-enabled processes. The findings further emphasize the importance of early planning for data integration, sensing requirements, performance evaluation, and interdisciplinary coordination. The study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on digital twin applications in architectural design by providing an evidence-based assessment of current adoption, opportunities, and challenges, offering practical insights for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers seeking to advance Building Lifecycle Management through digital transformation.

papers.title: Design and development of a test bench for railway coupler testing
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part F Journal of Rail and Rapid Transit
papers.abstract: Accurate modelling and experimental characterization of railway coupling devices are essential to reliably estimate the maximum longitudinal compressive and tensile forces to which a trainset is subjected. These estimates are paramount to ensure safe and efficient operations, particularly for longer and heavier freight trains. However, traditional testing of couplers is based on simple, standardized tests which fail to correctly reproduce their behaviour under realistic conditions. Moreover, these methodologies cannot be easily interfaced with numerical simulation tools. This paper presents the design and development of an innovative test bench for the experimental analysis of several types of railway couplers. The test bench can actuate a moving frame with two translational and one rotational degree of freedom in the horizontal plane, allowing indoor reproduction of relative motions between adjacent wagons. The bench is compatible with both conventional buffer-and-hook systems and Digital Automatic Couplers (DACs) and is equipped with a comprehensive measurement system for forces, moments, and displacements. The effects of uncertainties on the measurement setup are also discussed. The capabilities of the test bench are assessed through an experimental campaign on a standard UIC coupling system assembly, including compression and traction tests up to realistic load levels and an open-loop simulation of a trainset negotiating a double switch. The proposed test bench represents a flexible and effective tool for advanced experimental characterization of railway couplers and a solid basis for future Hardware-in-the-Loop based longitudinal dynamics investigations.

papers.title: Multi-response prediction and tension warning for a dual-rotor TLP wind turbine
papers.abstract: To improve short-term multi-response prediction for a dual-rotor tension-leg-platform wind turbine, multi-source time-series data were generated using STAR-CCM + under regular-wave, irregular-wave, and an additional representative wind–wave–current condition. A parallel feature-fusion PF-TCN-GRU model was developed to jointly predict heave, pitch, and TLP2 tension by combining multi-scale local features extracted by TCN with temporal dependencies learned by GRU. The model achieved R 2 values above 0.997 under regular waves and average R 2 values of 0.9297 and 0.9239 under the two baseline irregular-wave cases. Under the additional wind–wave–current condition, the average R 2 remained 0.9284. Comparative and repeated-run tests showed that PF-TCN-GRU remained competitive with the closest PF-CNN-GRU baseline, although the difference was not statistically significant. Prediction accuracy decreased as the horizon increased from 1 to 4 s, with pitch showing the greatest sensitivity. The TLP2-based P95 warning achieved a precision of 1.000 and a recall of 0.314. The results demonstrate the potential of PF-TCN-GRU for short-term coupled-response prediction and statistical tension-anomaly identification, while further experimental or field validation is still required.

papers.title: A Comparative Analysis of the Seismic Performance of Four Buildings Representative of Bagan’s Monumental Heritage
papers.abstract: This paper presents the outcomes of nonlinear static pushover and time history analyses, using both recorded and simulated ground motion signals, on 3D finite element macro-models of four buildings representative of Bagan’s monumental heritage: Myin-pya-gu (1493), Zan-thi (east) (558), Tha-mu-ti-hpaya (844), and Kya-zin-hpaya (1219). The simulations are validated against the observed seismic damage in the 1975 and 2016 earthquakes. The results of the nonlinear finite element method (NLFEM) analyses are complemented by seismic rocking analysis conducted on nonstructural elements, such as spires, through nonlinear kinematic analysis. Analytical estimates of acceleration levels capable of causing shear failure in spires are provided, focusing on elements with a slenderness ratio that makes them vulnerable to shearing rather than rocking (i.e. flexure-controlled) failure modes. A comparative assessment of seismic performance is presented for the four buildings, highlighting the influence of plan symmetry and vertical continuity. These attributes are proposed as key criteria for selecting appropriate retrofit schemes to protect Bagan’s monuments against future seismic events.

papers.title: Beam layout design in shear wall structures using a diffusion model guided by rule-based masks
papers.abstract: Serving as critical load supports and transfer components in shear wall structures, beams require layout designs that balance mechanical rationality with architectural functionality constraints. Conventional design methods, which rely on engineers' expertise, are challenging to systematize and are inherently inefficient. Moreover, existing intelligent design algorithms have attempted to integrate constraints related to architectural space and mechanical topology while delivering sufficiently detailed outputs, ultimately resulting in suboptimal outcomes. To address these challenges, this study synthesizes engineering experience rules pertaining to spatial functionality and load-bearing constraints and encodes them into a mask that delineates potential beam placement locations on a building plan. Subsequently, a diffusion model, well-known for its ability to generate intricate design details, is employed to produce the corresponding beam layout from the image mask. This approach, designated as the mask-constrained diffusion model for beam layout design in shear wall structures, introduces a key innovation: mitigating the uncontrolled generative range typically associated with diffusion models during beam layout configuration. By embedding engineering knowledge into a mask that constrains the diffusion process, the generation boundaries are effectively regulated, ensuring controllable and effective design outcomes. Analysis indicates that the designs produced by the mask-constrained diffusion model surpass the quality of existing intelligent design methods, achieving a relative 35.0% improvement in consistency with engineer-generated designs while concurrently satisfying critical mechanical performance criteria. This study provides a novel perspective on the intelligent design of beam layouts and serves as a valuable reference for the application of diffusion models in the structural design of buildings.

papers.title: Patterns and Impacts of OHS Risks among Plumbers in Australia: Insights from 15 Years of National Workers’ Compensation Data
papers.journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: Abstract Plumbers face several occupational health and safety (OHS) risks in the construction industry. However, existing evidence is largely fragmented, dated, or limited to prevalence-based assessments. This study addresses this gap by analyzing recent long-term (15 years, 2009–2023) workers’ compensation data from the Australian construction sector to examine the prevalence, severity, and mechanisms of both physical injuries and occupational diseases among plumbers. Descriptive statistical and two-way and three-way chi-square contingency analyses were performed to examine how incident severity varies across injury and disease types, incident mechanisms and agencies, affected body parts, worker demographics, and organizational size. The study found that physical injuries accounted for 80% of all incidents, and musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) and noise-induced hearing loss dominated health issues. Fatalities were primarily linked to asbestos-related diseases and electrocution, and permanent incapacities were driven by hearing loss, MSDs, and amputations. Plumbers accounted for nearly 10% of all construction incidents, with micro-businesses disproportionately affected, and apprentices represented 13% of cases. Noise-induced hearing loss emerged as the leading cause of permanent incapacity, highlighting underrecognized auditory risks. The study also identified 20 most common incident agencies and found strong associations between injury severity and affected body parts, particularly the head, neck, ears, back, shoulders, fingers, and knees. These findings advocate a trade-specific, priority-driven OHS risk management approach, accompanied by changes to policies and management practices related to noise exposure, ergonomic risks, hazardous material handling, and work organization in small enterprises.
papers.ck_take: Australian construction's risk management maturity gap is a wake-up call — data shows most firms are still reactive rather than proactively managing project risks.

papers.title: From Automation to Coevolution: A Systematic Review of Human–AI Interaction Hierarchies and Professional Implications in the Construction Industry
papers.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly reshaping the construction industry, creating increasing reliance on human–AI interaction across project processes. Although previous research has made significant progress in applying AI across construction workflows, existing literature reviews lack a systematic analysis of human–AI interaction patterns, coupling depths, and the implications for professional competence. To close this gap, this study aims to (1) systematize the hierarchical levels of human–AI interaction in construction applications; and (2) identify the professional competence requirements corresponding to different interaction levels. A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided systematic review was conducted, covering 57 peer-reviewed studies from 2016 to 2025, complemented by bibliometric mapping and thematic synthesis to identify patterns of interaction and competence demand in construction contexts. The review proposes a four-layer hierarchical framework of human–AI interaction: AI automation (Layer 1), AI assistance (Layer 2), AI–human coordination (Layer 3), and adaptive coevolution (Layer 4). Layers 1–3 emerged from empirical analysis of construction practice, and Layer 4 represents an emergent stage informed by nascent construction technologies and cross-domain coevolution frameworks. Each layer reflects distinct coupling intensity, interaction dynamics, and competence requirements. Building on these insights, this study proposes a human–AI interaction literacy matrix that systematically maps distinct levels of interaction depth to evolving professional competence requirements across technical-operational, analytical-evaluative, collaborative-interactional, and reflective-adaptive dimensions. These findings provide actionable guidance for construction organizations to design role-differentiated training programs aligned with interaction depth, assess workforce readiness for AI integration at specific project phases, and develop career pathways as human–AI interaction evolves from automation-dominant to collaboration-intensive configurations. The framework redefines AI adoption as a competence-driven progression rather than a purely technological implementation.

papers.title: In Situ Instrumentation and Calibration of Flexible Pavement Under Real Traffic: Experimental Comparison with the AEMC/MeDiNa Model in Brazil
papers.journal: International Journal of Pavement Research and Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract This article presents the design, calibration and field evaluation of an instrumented flexible pavement section aimed at quantifying mechanical responses and comparing them with the predictions of multilayer elastic analysis (AEMC), the mechanistic component of the Brazilian mechanistic-empirical method MeDiNa. Total earth pressure cells and strain gauges were installed in the asphalt layer, base, sub-base and subgrade to monitor stresses and strains under a controlled loading protocol ranging from 0 to 100% of the 8.2-ton standard axle load, to evaluate conversion factors and verify the metrological stability of the measurements. The results showed physically consistent time histories, with progressive response reduction as the load decreased, spatial sensitivity to wheel path position and stress attenuation with depth. In the model-to-field comparison, the assumptions of full and partial interlayer bonding generally provided better agreement with the measured data than the unbonded scenario, although magnitude discrepancies persisted for some stresses and strains. From an operational standpoint, the study highlighted the critical influence of sensor integrity and redundancy, cable and connection protection and vehicle trajectory control on data quality. As a contribution, the work provides experimental evidence for the evaluation of AEMC/MeDiNa in the Brazilian context and organizes practical recommendations for future instrumentation campaigns and for strengthening the regional calibration of the method.

papers.title: A kinematically-constrained Hankel dynamic mode decomposition for short-term prediction of ship manoeuvring in ambient currents
papers.abstract: The accurate prediction of vessel manoeuvring dynamics is essential for ensuring navigational safety in the transition toward maritime autonomy. In this study, a kinematically-constrained Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (Hankel-DMD) approach is developed to model and predict vessel manoeuvring dynamics. The vessel motion is represented using a state formulation consisting of position and resultant speed, and the Hankel-DMD method, together with a component-wise normalisation of the position states, is used to extract the modes governing the system dynamics. To improve the physical consistency of the prediction, a kinematic constraint linking vessel position and speed is incorporated as a post-processing reconstruction step. The developed approach is examined using the data generated from a physics-based Maneuvering Modelling Group (MMG) manoeuvring model for an azimuth thruster-equipped tug. Three cases are considered, including manoeuvring in calm water, in the presence of ambient current along the X -direction (following), and current along the Y -direction (cross). Quantitative error metrics show that the kinematically-constrained reconstruction reduces the trajectory RMSE by 71% in calm water (from 1.09 m to 0.31 m) and by 60% for the following current (from 7.31 m to 2.90 m). For the cross current, however, the XY-normalised pure Hankel-DMD prediction achieves the slightly lower RMSE (1.34 m versus 2.80 m for the constrained reconstruction), indicating that the benefit of the kinematic constraint is scenario-dependent. These findings demonstrate that incorporating a kinematic constraint can improve the robustness of data-driven vessel trajectory prediction, although its benefit is case-dependent under environmental disturbances.

papers.title: Contour Feature-Driven Deep Learning Method for Arch Dam Point Cloud Registration
papers.journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract The point cloud of an arch dam comprises two key target categories: the dam body and the bedrock. The bedrock exhibits complex, variable structures and anisotropic surface textures, presenting significant differences from the artificially constructed arch dam. To fully capture the distinctive features of both target types and enhance the registration accuracy of the arch dam, this paper proposes a deep learning-based point cloud registration method driven by arch dam contour features. This approach first addresses the substantial differences in surface features between dam body and rock mass by proposing a contour feature extraction method based on the transformer framework and collaborative clustering. This method separately acquires the contours of both the dam body and rock mass. Subsequently, to overcome the information loss during dimensionality reduction of high-dimensional features by traditional multilayer perceptron, which leads to estimation errors in the transformation matrix and causes local misalignment or global offset in registration results, this paper calculates 12-dimensional feature vectors from the positional relationships between points as input to the registration network. A channel attention mechanism combining average, max, and random pooling is constructed to extract deeper point cloud features from the arch dam data. Finally, a rigid transformation estimation network computes the transformation matrix. The proposed contour feature extraction method captures richer details for registration. Ablation experiments demonstrate that incorporating the feature extractor reduces rock mass and dam registration errors from 24.08 and 23.9 m to 0.71 and 0.64 m, respectively. Following the introduction of the multipooling attention mechanism, the errors were further reduced to 0.0181 and 0.0169 m, respectively. The proposed method provides a robust data foundation for detailed three-dimensional modeling and high-precision deformation detection.
